summary: Unmistakably the same pattern — a handful of randomly-coloured 3D balls bouncing inside a cube, drawn with an identical soft diamond falloff — with all three dials matching in direction and magnitude; the port diverges by being time-based where the original is frame-stepped, by never fully stopping at Speed=0, and by exposing two differently-named controls.
observations: Shared look (16x16 grid rig, untouched and dialed): both sides draw a small number of compact, fully-saturated blobs of random hue on pure black, drifting in straight lines and reflecting off the walls; the cloud rig (10x10x10, --label cloud) shows both sides producing the same 3D comet-trace texture, so both really are moving in 3D.

Ball rendering is essentially identical: a --dump of a single ball at Size=0.6 gives orig peak 250 with orthogonal neighbours 154/135/195 and port peak 249 with 134/189/172 — same diamond-shaped falloff, same peak level, same 3-4 px footprint.

Bouncing confirmed on both: a single-ball 30 s run (--label oneball) collapses to a clean zigzag in the rhythm image on each side, i.e. constant-velocity travel with hard wall reflections and no damping.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING (main divergence). Same dialed config at 10/20/40 fps (--label fps-10/20/40): the original's per-frame motion stat is flat at 12.8 / 13.2 / 13.2 while the port's falls 19.9 / 13.3 / 7.6 (~1/fps). Positional confirmation with a tracked single ball (--label pos-f10 / pos-f40): the original's centroid moves ~1.5 px/s at 10 fps and ~5.2 px/s at 40 fps (speed scales ~4x with fps = frame-stepped), while the port holds ~20 px/s at both rates (time-based). Net effect: the two agree on apparent speed only near 20 fps; at 5 fps the port runs several times faster than the original, at 40 fps several times slower.

Speed=0 does not stop the port. 30 s / 300 frames at Speed=0 (--label speed0-long): the original posts motion 0 on every frame (zeroMotionFrames 300) and a single ball's centroid is bit-identical for 6 s (--label sp0-pos: [5.13, 7.90] at every dump); the port posts motion avg 4.9 (zeroMotionFrames 1) and its ball keeps travelling ~2.5 px/s (centroid walks 14.25,12.60 -> 5.09,7.08 over 4 s). The port's Speed slider has a non-zero floor of roughly 0.15-0.2 in original units.
Size=0 leaves a residue on the port: original goes fully black (mean brightness 0.0), port sits at 0.3 with an occasional single lit pixel (--label sz-0).

Untouched defaults differ in ball size, not in count. Over 8 sampled frames of a 30 s default run (--label dump-many): orig ~8 lit px/frame across ~5.5 blobs (~1.5 px per ball), port ~13 lit px/frame across ~4.6 blobs (~2.9 px per ball); mean brightness 3.1 vs 4.7 over the 60 s survey. The port's default Size sits around 0.4 in slider units where the original's sits near 0.28.

Control surface mismatch: same three sliders and same kinds, but two of three names/labels differ — original exposes sliderBalls ("Balls") / sliderSize ("Size") / sliderSpeed ("Speed"); port exposes sliderBallCount ("BallCount") / sliderBallSize ("BallSize") / sliderSpeed ("Speed").

Original-side quirk the port does not reproduce: when Balls is the ONLY control set (--label ctl-balls-*), the original's density saturates from v=0.375 upward — mean brightness pinned at exactly 4.1 for 0.375, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 with byte-identical dumps — while the port keeps scaling (2.7 / 5.3 / 6.9 / 8.9 / 11.6 / 14.6). Once Size (or Speed) is also set, the original scales normally, so this is a setter-interaction artefact on the original rather than a port defect; noting it because it is the one place untouched-vs-dialed disagree.

Colour character matches: over 120 s at matched dials (--label hue2) both sides spread ball hues broadly around the wheel and both sit at mean saturation 0.71-0.76 on black. Per-ball hues are random and therefore not aligned between sides; that is expected, not a finding.

Steady state matches: 120 s at 5 fps and a --skip 90 late window both show steady brightnessTrend, no decay, no saturation, no mode rotation, and no zero-motion frames on either side. The pattern has a single regime.

dials.name: Balls / BallCount
dials.origEffect: Ball density scales smoothly with the slider: mean brightness 1.4 / 6.9 / 12.3 / 16.6 / 20.4 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 (Size and Speed pinned at 0.5), i.e. one ball at 0 rising to roughly a dozen visible balls at 1.
dials.portEffect: Same curve: 1.4 / 8.7 / 13.8 / 17.0 / 21.2 over the same settings; one ball at 0, slightly denser than the original at mid settings but tracking it closely.

dials.name: Size / BallSize
dials.origEffect: Ball radius grows monotonically: mean brightness 0.0 / 3.7 / 12.3 / 22.4 / 32.0 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1; at 0 nothing is drawn, at 1 balls are ~15-30 px blobs that frequently merge.
dials.portEffect: Near-identical: 0.3 / 5.0 / 13.8 / 23.6 / 32.4. Only difference is the floor — the port never reaches full black at Size=0.

dials.name: Speed
dials.origEffect: Monotonic speed control with a true stop: motion stat 0 / 7.4 / 13.1 / 16.1 / 18.3 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1. Speed=0 freezes every ball exactly in place.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and comparable range but offset upward and with no stop: 4.8 / 14.8 / 20.2 / 22.5 / 25.0. Speed=0 still drifts. (These per-frame numbers were taken at 10 fps; because of the frame-rate coupling above, the same sweep at 40 fps has the port below the original instead.)

feedback: Make the port's ball motion frame-stepped like the original instead of time-based. Measured: the original's ball speed scales with frame rate (~1.5 px/s at 10 fps, ~2.7 at 20 fps, ~5.2 at 40 fps on a 16x16 grid at Speed=0.5) while the port holds ~20 px/s at every rate. Calibrate so that at 20 fps the port matches its current speed, and so that halving/doubling the frame rate halves/doubles the on-screen speed as the original's does.

Give the Speed slider a true zero. At Speed=0 the original is completely frozen (mean per-frame motion exactly 0 over 300 frames); the port still moves its balls at ~2.5 px/s. Remove the constant floor so Speed=0 stops motion entirely, and re-check that the rest of the sweep still lands on the original's curve (original motion 0 / 7.4 / 13.1 / 16.1 / 18.3 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 measured at 10 fps).
Give the Size slider a true zero as well: at Size=0 the original renders pure black (mean brightness 0.0) while the port leaves a residual lit pixel (0.3).

Shrink the untouched default ball size by roughly 30% in radius. At default dials the original averages ~8 lit pixels per frame with ~1.5 px per ball; the port averages ~13 with ~2.9 px per ball, which makes the port read noticeably brighter and chunkier out of the box (mean brightness 4.7 vs 3.1). Default ball COUNT is already right — do not change it.

Rename the two mismatched controls to match the original's surface exactly: sliderBalls (label "Balls") and sliderSize (label "Size"), not sliderBallCount/sliderBallSize. Names and labels are user-visible and are what a saved pattern's stored slider values key off.

Everything else already matches and should not be touched: the per-ball brightness falloff (peak ~250 with ~135-195 orthogonal neighbours), the black background, the random fully-saturated per-ball hues spread around the whole wheel, the constant-velocity travel with hard wall reflections, the 3D behaviour visible on a cloud rig, and the Balls and Size response curves.
